title: Introduce timelag-aware eval smokehook and late-arrival reconciler
author: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: CI/eval jobs occasionally produce false-positive regressions when telemetry or ground-truth anchors arrive late (log shipping delays, async replay pipelines). These transient failures create noisy alerts and block rollouts.

What this PR does: introduces a timelag-aware smokehook and a lightweight late-arrival reconciler. The smokehook defers hard fail decisions for a configurable window (default 120s) when a cohort shows near-threshold regressions and will attempt to replay anchors as late telemetry becomes available. The reconciler incrementally consumes late anchor events and probabilistically re-evaluates only the affected examples to decide whether to suppress a CI failure or escalate it.

Design notes: single continuous string description but covers multiple components — hooks, reconciler, config, docs, and tests. Key behaviors: (1) deferral with backoff and capped retries, (2) probabilistic rehearse to bound compute cost, (3) opt-in per-pipeline via ci_hooks/timelag-ci.yaml, (4) metrics emitted for deferred_count, reconciled_true_positive, reconciled_false_positive, and mean_reconcile_latency.

Backward compatibility: smokehook is disabled by default; opt-in via Linear ticket or YAML flag. No breaking API changes.

Usage example (pseudo):
  - enable: ci_hooks.timelag.defer_enabled=true
  - window: ci_hooks.timelag.defer_window_sec=120
  - policy: ci_hooks.timelag.reconcile_policy=probabilistic(0.2)

Rationale: We observed ~6% of rolling-eval failures were explained by anchors arriving >30s after job completion in the last month. This change reduces noise while preserving a prompt escalation path for genuine regressions.
